payload.claim: `_layer_findings`'s docstring and design claim that a generation-1 layer's critic entries (`_left_by_critic`) always keep `pushed_sha`, 'critic entries included', regardless of `heads`. The only new witness that exercises `heads` (`test_each_finding_names_the_head_the_end_review_graded_its_layer_at`) never names the generation-1 layer (`TE-20`) in `heads` for either call, so it cannot distinguish the current explicit `layer["pushed_sha"]` argument from a version that instead consults `heads` for that same call. Replacing `layer["pushed_sha"]` with `heads.get(task_key, layer["pushed_sha"])` on this line keeps every current test green (no test ever puts TE-20's task key in `heads`), yet it silently makes critic entries respect a graded head if one were ever recorded for a generation-1 layer, contradicting the function's own stated guarantee. The gap is currently benign only because of the separate invariant that generation-1 layers are never graded; the witness does not itself prove the guarantee the docstring states.
